solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Is having to reflect about poor treatment

indicators.note: placed about something, the pondering word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to muse is to reflect or ponder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person troubled by having to look back on how badly they were treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflect' looks like the action of a mirror, but here it means to ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuse or mistreatment of something is a synonym for poor treatment of it.

clue.text: Day and time no illusion in city in 21

parts.note: Mon is the short form of Monday
what is real is no illusion

explanation.surface: A day spent in a Canadian city is no dream at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Montreal is the largest city in Quebec province, an example of a Canadian city.

clue.text: Going about clumsily in fake jewellery

parts.note: a sham is a fake
bling is showy, flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone lumbering around dripping in costume jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking in an awkward, shuffling, ungainly way, moving about clumsily.

clue.text: Constituent in South Africa's ancient city

indicators.note: the constituent is put inside the country letters

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
a part is a constituent of a whole

explanation.surface: A voter in South Africa belongs to an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituent' suggests a voter but means a component.
explanation.definitionFit: The warlike city-state of classical Greece is an example of an ancient city.

clue.text: Secret drinker last to rise in Morecambe?

indicators.note: the last letter belonging to the word rise is wanted here

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drinker
Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, so his first name is suggested by the question mark

explanation.surface: A hidden boozer is the last to get up in a seaside town in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire seaside town, but it stands for comedian Eric Morecambe, of the British double act Morecambe and Wise. 'last to' picks E from 'rise', which goes before SOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something known only to an initiated few is arcane, a close synonym of secret.

clue.text: No to musicians becoming self- righteous

indicators.note: the letters turn into, or become, a new word

explanation.surface: Turning down the band makes someone smug and holier-than-thou.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a show of moral superiority, priggish, a synonym of self-righteous.

clue.text: Use horn on French street? Yes indeed!

parts.note: to toot is to sound a horn
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: Honking on a Paris boulevard, and someone heartily agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Said in rueful agreement that something is only too accurate, an emphatic yes.

clue.text: Headless chicken or blackbird?

indicators.note: the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: chicken means cowardly, as does craven
C is the head, the first letter, cut from the word meaning cowardly

explanation.surface: Is that a decapitated hen or a dark songbird?
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' is the adjective cowardly, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large glossy black corvid, so literally a black bird, though not the thrush of that name.

clue.text: We're made up with this vehicle, good in Paris

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
bon is French for good

explanation.surface: Someone happily finished off with a car that is good in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' reads like pleased or wearing cosmetics, but it means composed of.
explanation.definitionFit: All living things are carbon-based, so this element is what our bodies are made from.

clue.text: Gangster in New York area is beast

indicators.note: the gangster is placed inside the city and area letters

parts.note: Al Capone, the archetypal gangster, gives AL

explanation.surface: A mobster in a New York district is a real animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned African antelope, an example of a beast.

clue.text: Lead shield surrounds Uranium City in 21

parts.note: the van is the leading part of an army or movement

indicators.note: the shielding word goes all round the element symbol

parts.note: a cover shields what is under it
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A protective lead casing encloses a radioactive town.
explanation.walkthrough: Uranium City is a real town in Saskatchewan, a nice decoy: here the city is the answer, and 21 is CANADA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a major port on the Pacific coast of British Columbia, an example of a Canadian city.

clue.text: Award winner — first clue in the puzzle!

parts.note: a victor is a winner
the first clue is One Across, written with the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A prizewinner proclaims the opening clue of this crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Award winner' runs together on the surface, but the definition is 'Award' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest British and Commonwealth military decoration for valour, an example of an award.

clue.text: Old boy, in tight trio, cold like mechanical man

indicators.note: the old boy letters go inside the rearranged trio
tight is slang for drunk, so the trio's letters are reeling about

parts.note: OB is the usual abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A former pupil, squeezed into a close threesome and cold, behaves like an automaton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' scrambles the trio into ROTI before the old boy goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembling an automaton or android, stiff and mechanical in manner.

clue.text: Lone Ranger's companion entertains men in state capital

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them inside, so the companion's name holds the men

parts.note: Tonto was the Lone Ranger's sidekick in the Western series
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: The masked cowboy's sidekick plays host to a group of men.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the capital of the province of Ontario, loosely a state capital.

clue.text: Sharp Conservative to cut help for developing countries?

indicators.note: the party letter cuts into the help word, splitting it

parts.note: foreign aid is help given to poorer nations

explanation.surface: A cutting Tory sets out to slash overseas aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart, biting taste or remark is a synonym of sharp.

clue.text: Incoherent and lacking class?

parts.note: in British schools a form is a class of pupils
less, as a suffix, means lacking or without

explanation.surface: A rambling, shapeless argument that also lacks any sophistication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' looks like style or refinement, but it is a school class, a form.
explanation.definitionFit: Without shape or structure, so vague and lacking coherence.

clue.text: Duskiness developing? Here's why!

indicators.note: a developing thing is changing form, so the letters re-form

explanation.surface: Getting darker skin? This is the reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tanned by the sun is exactly why skin grows dusky.

clue.text: Hybrid pig new in state capital

indicators.note: a hybrid mixes things up, so these letters are combined anew

explanation.surface: A crossbred pig makes its debut in a regional capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnipeg is the capital of the province of Manitoba, loosely a state capital.

clue.text: Fuel GT carrying Scotsman's massive body

parts.note: gas is a fuel

indicators.note: the car letters carry the man's name within them

parts.note: taken as written, GT being a gran turismo car
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A fuel-guzzling sports car carries a burly Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Planets like Jupiter and Saturn, made largely of hydrogen and helium, are huge celestial bodies.

clue.text: Guy from Barcelona maybe clutching at politician

indicators.note: the Spanish gentleman clutches the little word, holding it inside

parts.note: senor is Spanish for a man or gentleman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish man grabs at a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a senate is an example of a politician.

clue.text: Political opponent one seen by social worker

parts.note: ants are social insects that labour for the colony
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A political rival gets spotted with a council care worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a welfare officer but the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is against a policy or party, an opponent, as a noun.

clue.text: Ring up a Scottish engineer in 21's capital

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like O

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words are read from the bottom

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer behind the steam engine

explanation.surface: Phone a Scottish engineer living in the Canadian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring up' looks like phone, but 'Ring' is O and 'up' turns A + WATT into TTAWA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the national capital of Canada, the answer to 21.

clue.text: Country's miraculous place diaspora vacated

parts.note: Cana is where Jesus turned water into wine

indicators.note: with its inside emptied out, only the outside letters remain

explanation.surface: A nation is a wondrous place that its scattered people left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a nation of North America, an example of a country.

clue.text: Extremely large attic in for conversion

indicators.note: converting a loft rearranges it, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A huge loft lined up for a conversion project.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal or gigantic, a synonym of extremely large, from the mythical giants.

clue.text: Roman banker and bishop involved in row

indicators.note: the bishop is wrapped up inside the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A Roman financier and a bishop are caught up in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is not a financier but a river, which has banks; 'row' is a tier, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing through Rome has banks, making it a crossword-style banker.

clue.text: Formal speech on about relationship

indicators.note: the little word is placed about the other, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
a ratio is a numerical relationship between quantities

explanation.surface: An official address on the subject of a partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal public address, such as a funeral or ceremonial speech.

clue.text: Baggage southern family brought back to Scotland

indicators.note: the reversed piece is joined on to the end of the Gaelic name

parts.note: Alba is the Gaelic name for Scotland

indicators.note: the southern letter and family word are brought back, read backwards

parts.note: a sort is a kind or family of things

explanation.surface: Luggage of a family from the south gets brought back to Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns S + SORT into TROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotional burden one cannot shake off, figurative baggage, from the bird in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner.

clue.text: Fabulist initially allowed revolutionary attitude

indicators.note: only the first letter of allowed is wanted
a revolution turns things round, so the attitude word is read backwards

parts.note: a pose is an attitude struck

explanation.surface: A storyteller at first permitted a rebellious stance.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek writer of moral fables, a famous teller of fables.

clue.text: Song book with which rockers from 12 improve image

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
Rush is a rock band from Toronto, the answer to 12 across

explanation.surface: A song and a book used by a band to polish their public image.
explanation.definitionFit: Retouching a photograph with a spray tool improves the picture's look.

clue.text: Sycophant in Californian force taking westbound journey

indicators.note: the police force takes on the following piece

parts.note: LAPD is the Los Angeles Police Department

indicators.note: in an across clue, westbound means read right to left

parts.note: a go is a turn or trip, as in going somewhere

explanation.surface: A toady in the Los Angeles police goes on a trip west.
explanation.definitionFit: A fawning follower, someone servile like a pet dog, is a sycophant.
